blogs.title: Biting Into Sepsis: Recognizing Capnocytophaga canimorsus After Dog Bites
blogs.description: A deep dive into the epidemiology, clinical spectrum and diagnostic pitfalls of Capnocytophaga canimorsus infection. We will explore why this fastidious gram‑negative rod often masquerades as ordinary sepsis, review bite‑related risk factors (including missed prophylaxis), compare traditional culture techniques with modern molecular tools such as real‑time nanopore sequencing, and discuss empiric antimicrobial regimens that reliably cover zoonotic pathogens while awaiting definitive identification.

blogs.title: Septic TMA Unraveled: Distinguishing DIC, TTP, STEC‑HUS & Complement‑Mediated HUS
blogs.description: When a septic patient develops hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury, the differential widens dramatically. This post walks readers through a step‑by‑step algorithm that incorporates bedside clues (e.g., skin findings, bleeding pattern), laboratory panels (ADAMTS13 activity, PLASMIC score, Shiga toxin PCR), and time course considerations to separate disseminated intravascular coagulation from true thrombotic microangiopathies such as TTP, STEC‑HUS and atypical (complement‑mediated) HUS.

blogs.title: Beyond C3/C4: Advanced Complement Testing to Diagnose Complement‑Mediated HUS
blogs.description: Normal C3/C4 levels frequently mislead clinicians when evaluating suspected atypical HUS. This article explains functional complement assays (AH50, alternative pathway activity), factor H/I/B measurements and anti‑factor H antibody testing, illustrating how they can uncover hidden dysregulation even when standard serology is unrevealing. We will contextualize these tests with the patient’s case where extended complement workup was pivotal despite unremarkable baseline labs.

blogs.title: Eculizumab in the Time of Infection: Timing, Vaccination & Prophylaxis When Treating CM‑HUS
blogs.description: Launching terminal complement blockade amid an active bacterial infection poses a therapeutic dilemma. This piece reviews current guidance on when to start eculizumab versus using plasma exchange as a bridge, outlines mandatory meningococcal vaccination schedules and antibiotic prophylaxis strategies for patients receiving complement inhibitors, and discusses risk mitigation for encapsulated organisms—including Capnocytophaga—using real‑world data from cases similar to the one reported.

blogs.title: Kidney Biopsy Decodes Thrombotic Microangiopathy—Histologic Clues that Guide Therapy
blogs.description: Renal pathology can differentiate overlapping TMAs when clinical data are ambiguous. We will dissect the hallmark light microscopy findings of DIC‑related cortical necrosis versus fibrin thrombi in glomeruli/crescents typical for complement‑mediated HUS, illustrate the role of immunofluorescence and electron microscopy in ruling out immune complex disease, and explain how biopsy results directly influence decisions such as proceeding to eculizumab versus continuing plasma exchange.
